craft_notes: Sthāyin: inversion (fault-become-no-fault). Device: comma→question (taint asked), kept closing dash (greed lands). Upaya belongs to Ksemaraja, never the root — stated in argmap only. Rejected: 'stain' for 'taint' — killed: taint clings, stain washes; kept. Read aloud: lands on close.

lines: What taint is taint in souls set to attain thee, e'en Lord?
what worth is worth, pray, in souls set never to attain? Be passion mine, world-Lord, on thee alone reposed — yea, homage to my greed, leashed to gain of thee.
l4.sanskrit_cite: doṣo 'pideva ko doṣas tvām āptuṃ yaḥ samāsthitaḥ guṇo 'pi ca guṇaḥ ko nu tvāṃ nāptuṃ yaḥ samāsthitaḥ rāgo 'py astu jagannātha mama tvayy eva yaḥ sthitaḥ lobhāyāpi namas tasmai tvallābhālambanāya me

reads_against.argmap: What fault is fault in one set on reaching you? What virtue in one set on not reaching?; Let passion be mine resting in you alone; bow even to my greed whose prop is gaining you. (Upāya reading belongs to Kṣemarāja, never the root.) → Fault aimed at you is no fault; even greed for you is bow-worthy.
c1_essence: Fault reaching you turns faultless; greed for you turns worshipful.
reads_against.c1_rasa: bhakti with audārya (generosity tasted and returned)
reads_against.l2: What blame is blame in a man bent on winning you, even O god? What worth is worth, pray, in a man bent on never winning you? Be passion mine, world-lord, fastened on you alone — and homage even to my greed, leashed to gaining you.
